subject: Re: MAP - benchmarking scoping, eval plan & target close
messages:
From: Alicia Moreno <alicia.moreno@gammahealth.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@gammahealth.com
Date: 2026-09-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: MAP kickoff: performance benchmarking scope request

Hi Jonas,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team is excited about Redwood. To get internal sign-off we need a concrete MAP section for performance: scope of benchmark, what you will run, success criteria (esp. TTFT and 95th/99th latency), expected throughput/concurrency, and a proposed acceptance window so we can close by our procurement deadlines.

Key constraints: live HL7-ish payloads (avg prompt ~480 tokens, 90th pct 1.2k), peak concurrency expected ~180 simultaneous sessions, and we need TTFT <= 250ms p50 for interactive triage flows.

Can you send a short plan and propose dates for test execution and final review?

Best,
Alicia
Alicia Moreno
Director, Clinical Operations
Gamma Health

Attachments: sample-payloads.json (referenced)

From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: Alicia Moreno <alicia.moreno@gammahealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-01T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff: performance benchmarking scope request

Alicia — thanks for the clear constraints. Drafting a concise MAP appendix for performance; high level below. I’ll attach a worksheet for you to confirm traffic slices. Proposed execution window: Sept 6–7 (load tests) with a Sept 8 review.

Summary plan (short):
- Workload definition: three slices (interactive triage, batch summarization, embedding lookup). We’ll model prompt length distribution based on your sample (avg 480, 90th 1.2k).
- Test matrix: vary concurrency (50/100/180), sequence lengths (avg/90th), and model variants (redwood-llamaq8-small, redwood-7b-8q).
- Metrics captured: TTFT (p50/p90/p95), token-level latency (p50/p90/p95), throughput (requests/sec), model cost estimate per 1M tokens, error rate and tail variance, memory/CPU telemetry.
- Success criteria (pass/fail): interactive triage TTFT p50 <= 250ms and p95 <= 750ms; sustained throughput >= 120 rps at target concurrency for batching flows; <1% error rate for generation timeouts.
- Acceptance: sign-off if all critical slices meet criteria OR if automatic fallback plan keeps user-visible TTFT under 500ms (degraded mode) and product team accepts tradeoffs.

Deliverables: load scripts, raw telemetry CSVs (ttft_results.csv), consolidated summary with pass/fail per slice, and a short runbook for production rollout.

I attached the MAP worksheet (gamma_map_v1.xlsx) with the slices. If that looks right we’ll lock the test window.

-Jonas

Jonas Weber
Head of Solutions Engineering — Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.ai
(attachment: gamma_map_v1.xlsx)

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-03T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff: performance benchmarking scope request

Adding the execution details and the exact test recipes we plan to run — please review.

Test recipes (engineer notes):
- Slice A (interactive triage): 60% of requests; prompt length dist: 300–600 tokens (mean 480). Target concurrency: 50 / 100 / 180. Mode: streaming enabled; TTFT capture at network egress.
- Slice B (batch summarization): 30% requests; prompt length 1k–1.5k; batch size 8; target throughput aim 120 rps sustained.
- Slice C (embedding + retrieval): 10% requests; small prompt 40–120 tokens; high QPS for vector lookups.

Instrumentation: continuous batching enabled where possible; play with KV cache warm/cold conditions; run each recipe for 30 minutes to reach steady state. For TTFT we capture p50/p90/p95 and also a moving 5-minute window.

Data to produce: ttft_results.csv (per-second TTFT), concurrency_profile.log, cost_estimate.md. I’ll run the initial baseline on Redmond cluster (dGPU A100 equiv).

-Marissa

(attachment: concurrency_load_profile.json)

From: Alicia Moreno <alicia.moreno@gammahealth.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@gammahealth.com, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-06T17:16:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff: performance benchmarking scope request

Thanks for the plan. Two clarifications before you run: (1) for regulated data we’ll use anonymized HL7 — confirm that logs will be scrubbed and stored per our retention policy (we need 12 months), and (2) procurement asked that results include a deterministic recommendation for Dedicated vs Hosted based on cost/perf at our concurrency.

If you can confirm both, go ahead with Sept 6 runs. We’re aiming to review results and lock procurement by Sept 10.

Best,
Alicia

P.S. cc-ing your ops contact Laura to confirm retention/KMS plan.

From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: Alicia Moreno <alicia.moreno@gammahealth.com>, procurement@gammahealth.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-08T16:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff: performance benchmarking scope request — results and next steps

Team — quick summary of the Sept 6–7 runs and recommended closure path. Raw CSVs attached (ttft_results.csv). Full workbook is at the Drive link in the MAP.

Executive summary:
- Run configuration: redwood-7b-8q (primary) and redwood-llamaq8-small (fallback). Tests run on HW equivalent to 8xA100; KV cache warm and cold captured separately. Each recipe ran 30 minutes steady-state.

Key results (interactive triage slice, avg prompt ~480):
- TTFT (redwood-7b-8q): p50 = 210ms, p90 = 410ms, p95 = 630ms.
- Token-level latency p50/p90/p95 = 6ms / 18ms / 34ms per token.
- Sustained concurrency: at 180 concurrent sessions we observed throughput ~135 rps with 1.2% timeouts during the cold-KV window. Warm-KV sustained 150 rps at 180 concurrency.

Batch summarization slice (avg 1.2k):
- Sustained throughput target (120 rps) achieved on the 7b-8q model with batching=8; CPU/GPU utilization within expected envelopes.

Pass/fail against acceptance criteria:
- Interactive triage: PASS for p50 <= 250ms (210ms) and marginal at p95 (630ms <= 750ms) — PASS.
- Throughput: PASS (>=120 rps) for batching flows.
- Error rate: overall 1.2% including cold-cache timeouts (slightly above 1% threshold).

Recommendations:
1) Production configuration: start Hosted with redwood-7b-8q and prefix/KV cache warmers for critical triage flows; set autoscale policy to maintain warm-KV hot slices during business hours.
2) If procurement requires a Dedicated cost estimate, we recommend Dedicated for 99% tail-sensitive workloads — attached cost delta and decision matrix (worksheet tab). Hosted remains acceptable with small fallbacks and offers faster time-to-production.
3) Next steps & close timeline: we propose sending you the final MAP appendix and a short statement of results today; procurement review closes on Sept 10. If accepted, onboarding and Dedicated sizing kickoff scheduled Sept 20.

Action items for Gamma Health:
- Confirm acceptance of PASS criteria and whether you require Dedicated pricing for an internal decision (procurement deadline Sept 10).
- Confirm log retention and KMS requirements (Laura is looped).

I’ll upload the final MAP appendix and supporting CSVs to the Drive and mark the MAP as ready-for-review in HubSpot (link included).

Thanks — happy to jump on a 30-min readout if useful.

-Jonas

(attachments: ttft_results.csv, mutual_action_plan.docx)
